items.title: Add a preview ledger-write result contract
items.summary: Adds the 2026-07-31-preview version and versions the ledger-write response into a transaction-id response wrapper plus a body model containing collectionId, optional receipt and application claims, and required transaction state; it also adds a typed 503 rollback error while preserving the earlier result model for older API versions.

inferenceResults.rationale: The renamed historical response model is explicitly retained for versions before 2026-07-31-preview; the hunk itself does not remove a wire member or public SDK symbol in the selected target contract.
Adding the chronologically later preview version and marking it with @Azure.Core.previewVersion selects a new API surface without changing existing version contracts.

lines: * Returned as a result of a write to the Confidential Ledger, the transaction id
* in the response indicates when the write will become durable.
+ * Returned as a result of writing to the Confidential Ledger.
+ * The result of writing a ledger entry.
+   * The collection identifier of the ledger entry.
+   * The receipt certifying the committed transaction.
+ * The transaction was rolled back before it could be committed.
* The result of querying for a ledger entry from an older transaction id. The
* ledger entry is available in the response only if the returned state is Ready.

guidance.section: Adding, removing, and renaming API elements
guidance.excerpt: Versioning allows you to evolve your API without breaking existing clients. By using versioning decorators, you can specify when resources, operations, or properties are added, removed, or changed.
examples: Use @added for new models and properties, @removed for elements absent from the new version, and @renamedFrom for renamed declarations.
